messages:
sophie: heads up — noticed a weird scheduling issue after the latest chart change: our gpu workload is sometimes landing on CPU nodes and getting OOMKilled. Repro in staging.

sophie: quick dump of rendered podSpec from helm template in CI: 
```yaml
spec:
  nodeSelector: null
  tolerations: []
```
If nodeSelector is null k8s ignores it and scheduler picks wrong nodes.

raja: sounds like values coalescing bug — we expect an empty map `{}` when no nodeSelector is supplied, not `null`. Which helper produced this? `values.nodeSelector` directly?

raja: common culprit is using `{{- if .Values.nodeSelector }}` in templates; when values is set to `null` that conditional fails and you end up rendering `nodeSelector: {{ .Values.nodeSelector }}` which produces `null` text.

marc: CI shows chart-testing step passed `helm lint` but a downstream `helm template` step (our render gate) returned the `null`. Lint doesn't catch `null` vs `{}` problems.

marc: suggested quickfix in chart helper `helpers.tpl`: add a safe coalesce helper like:
```gotemplate
{{- define "redwood.safeMap" -}}
{{- $v := . -}}
{{- if or (eq $v nil) (eq $v "") }}{}{{- else }}{{- toYaml $v | nindent 2 }}{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```
Then in pod template: `nodeSelector: {{ include "redwood.safeMap" .Values.nodeSelector }}`

yvonne: note: some teams populate values via Terraform remote state + secrets manager — the provider sometimes writes `null` for missing maps. We should handle that at chart level but also fix the values.schema.json to avoid accidental nulls.

marc: +1 on values schema update. Proposed schema snippet to catch null and non-object types:
```json
"nodeSelector": {
  "oneOf": [
    { "type": "object" },
    { "type": "null" }
  ]
}
```
But better: disallow null entirely so CI fails earlier:
```json
"nodeSelector": { "type": "object" }
```
This will break charts that intentionally send `null` though.

raja: I'd prefer defensive chart templates (safeMap) AND a stricter schema. Two layers: template ensures runtime safety, schema forces callers to fix values.

ci-bot: chart-render-check failed for branch `staging/helm-opts` — rendered pod has `nodeSelector: null` (See job logs: https://ci.redwood/mock/1234).

deploy-bot: automated canary rollout for `gpu-worker` was paused: 2/5 pods failed readiness due to OOMKilled after landing on CPU nodes. Manual rollback initiated.

sophie: plan: 1) merge `redwood.safeMap` helper + unit test in `charts/*/tests/render_test.go` that asserts `nodeSelector` renders as `{}`; 2) tighten values.schema.json to `type: object`; 3) update chart-testing CI to run `helm template` and a small jq-based assert to reject `null` fields; 4) add a gitops pre-apply check in the pipeline that validates rendered manifests before promoting to canary.

marc: I can open a tiny PR for the helper + tests. Will also add a linter rule in `.github/workflows/chart-lint.yml` to run `yq` check: `yq eval '.spec.nodeSelector == null'` and fail if true.

yvonne: FYI ops config team will audit terraform secret outputs for `null` vs `{}` and add a mapping step in the state exports to normalize maps to `{}`. Might be a slow rollout.

raja: long-term: maybe we should add a chart-testing policy plugin that rejects `null` for map-like fields automatically based on the schema. Could plug it into our gitops bot.

sophie: agreed. Short term I'll merge the helper fix and CI assert. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
